newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Nigerian troops reinforce Sierra Leone airport.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian troops reinforce Sierra Leone airport.

text.p: Nigerian troops of a regional peacekeeping force have reinforced Sierra Leone's international airport after Sunday's coup, aid workers and diplomats said on Tuesday.
At the same time, Sierra Leone's new military rulers issued a statement denying that Nigerian troops stationed in Sierra Leone under a regional defence accord planned an attack.

Aid workers and diplomats said the Nigerians arrived on Monday night at Lunghi, across the Sierra Leone River from Freetown, to reinforce Nigerians and Ghanaians of the ECOMOG force stationed at the airport to defend it from rebel attacks.

The airport and land borders have been closed since Sunday's coup. It was not immediately clear whether the troops formed part of reinforcements reported heading for Sierra Leone from neighbouring Liberia on Monday.

"The AFRC is concerned over rumours that our brothers, the Nigerian force, are about to launch an attack," said a statement on national radio from the chairman of the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council, Major Johnny Paul Koromah.

"The AFRC is hereby informing the general public to know that it is a baseless rumour. The situation is under control, and all and sundry are hereby requested to go about their normal duties," said the statement. Nigerian troops lead the ECOMOG West African peacekeeping force and were involved in fighting at the presidential offices in Freetown on Sunday.
